name: provisional
description: Provisional questions written from the iMac Product Environmental Report (Oct 2024) while official sample questions are unavailable. Expected answers were checked against the PDF text; page numbers are physical PDF pages (1-15).

schema.expected_status: answered | insufficient_evidence | either (abstaining or answering with must_include both count as correct)
schema.must_include: list of groups; every group must match; a group matches if any alternative appears in the answer (case-insensitive substring, or a regex when prefixed with 're:')
schema.expected_numbers: numbers that must appear in the answer (absolute value compared, tolerance tol)
schema.evidence_pages: list of page groups; each group must be covered by a retrieved/cited page; pages inside one group are alternatives
schema.acceptable_pages: extra pages that are legitimate to cite (not required)
schema.evidence_phrases: verbatim phrases from the PDF that the retrieved evidence must contain (whitespace, dashes and [^n] markers normalised)

questions.question: When was the iMac covered by this report introduced?
questions.expected_answer: October 28, 2024.

questions.question: How much less energy does iMac use than the ENERGY STAR requirement?
questions.expected_answer: 58 percent less energy than the ENERGY STAR requirement (endnote 18 gives the basis).

questions.question: In what share of the countries where Apple sells products does it provide or participate in product take-back and recycling collection programs?
questions.expected_answer: 99 percent of the countries where Apple sells products.

questions.question: Which ISO standards are Apple's product carbon footprint calculations performed in accordance with?
questions.expected_answer: ISO 14040, ISO 14044 and ISO 14067.

questions.question: How many components in iMac use at least 50 percent recycled plastic?
questions.expected_answer: 13 components.

questions.question: Over what period does Apple assume first owners use macOS devices when modelling product-use emissions?
questions.expected_answer: A four-year period (three years for iOS and watchOS devices).

questions.question: What percentage of the materials in iMac are covered by Apple's Regulated Substances Specification?
questions.expected_answer: 100 percent.
evidence_phrases: 100 percent of the materials in iMac

questions.question: What share of the makeup of iMac devices, by mass, does Apple identify?
questions.expected_answer: Over 80 percent by mass.

questions.question: What is iMac's power consumption in sleep mode at 115V?
What is the power adapter efficiency at 230V?
What is iMac's idle power consumption with the display on at 100V?
What share of the life cycle emissions of iMac (two ports) 256GB comes from product use?
What are Apple's scope 2 emissions from utility-purchased electricity for iMac (two ports) 256GB?
questions.expected_answer: 0 kg CO2e.

questions.question: What is the carbon footprint of iMac (four ports) 512GB?
questions.expected_answer: 391 kg CO2e.

questions.question: What share of iMac's life cycle carbon emissions comes from end-of-life processing?
questions.expected_answer: Less than 1% (<1%).

questions.question: In the 'Progress toward carbon neutral' chart, what are the baseline emissions and the final iMac emissions?
questions.expected_answer: Baseline emissions 445 kg; iMac emissions 346 kg (after -99 kg of reductions).

questions.question: How large are the emissions reductions shown in the iMac carbon emissions chart?
Which emissions-reduction categories are labelled in the progress toward carbon neutral chart?
questions.expected_answer: Recycled and low-carbon materials, low-carbon electricity (for manufacturing), electricity for product use, and non-air shipping.

questions.question: Why are renewable energy emissions not visible on the iMac carbon emissions chart?
questions.expected_answer: They are too small to be visible on the chart (endnote 11).

questions.question: According to the packaging infographic, what percentage of the packaging is fiber-based and how much recycled content does the fiber packaging contain?
questions.expected_answer: 100% fiber-based; 76% recycled content in fiber packaging.

questions.question: What values does the 'Energy consumption of ENERGY STAR-rated products' chart show?
questions.expected_answer: The chart's graphics and values are not present in this PDF (only its title remains); the report states iMac consumes 58 percent less energy than the ENERGY STAR requirement.
questions.notes: Limitation test: the chart did not survive in this PDF. Abstaining, or answering that values are unavailable while giving the 58% statement, are both correct.

questions.question: Does iMac's 'more than 15 percent recycled content' figure include packaging?
questions.expected_answer: No. Per endnote 1 it is the mass of certified recycled material relative to the device's overall mass, not including packaging or in-box accessories.
evidence_phrases: not including packaging or in-box accessories

questions.question: Is every Apple product completely free of PVC and phthalates?
questions.expected_answer: No. AC power cords in India, Thailand (2-prong) and South Korea are excepted, pending government approval of the replacement (endnote 5).

questions.question: Which iMac configuration does the recycled copper in the thermal module apply to?
questions.expected_answer: iMac (four ports) only (endnote 14).

questions.question: What is excluded from Apple's calculations of plastic content and packaging weight?
questions.expected_answer: Adhesives, inks and coatings (endnote 3).
evidence_phrases: Adhesives, inks, and coatings are excluded

questions.question: What does the Zero Waste to Landfill claim for iMac final assembly supplier sites require, and who verifies it?
questions.expected_answer: Established final assembly sites (Apple suppliers for more than one year) are third-party verified as Zero Waste by UL LLC (UL 2799); UL requires at least 90 percent diversion through methods other than waste to energy (endnote 16).

questions.question: For which recycled materials does Apple currently quantify carbon savings?
questions.expected_answer: Recycled aluminum, titanium, stainless steel, lithium, cobalt, tungsten and gold in select parts for select products (endnote 8).

questions.question: What EPEAT rating did iMac achieve, and in which countries?
questions.expected_answer: A Gold rating in the United States and Canada (endnote 6).
evidence_phrases: Gold rating in the United States and Canada

questions.question: Which iMac configuration is the 346 kg CO2e carbon footprint based on?
questions.expected_answer: The carbon footprint table (p12) and p2 attribute 346 kg CO2e to iMac (two ports) with 256GB. Note: endnote 10, attached to the chart's 346 kg 'iMac emissions', says the LCA is based on iMac (two ports) with 512GB, so the report is internally inconsistent.
questions.notes: Source inconsistency between p12/p2 (256GB) and endnote 10 (512GB). Mentioning both is ideal but only 256GB is required.

questions.question: By how much has Apple reduced iMac emissions, and what business-as-usual scenario are the reductions measured against?
questions.expected_answer: More than 20 percent (p2, p12) against a product-specific business-as-usual scenario modelled by Apple: no clean electricity beyond the grid, Apple's 2015 carbon intensity of key materials, and its average transport mode mix for fiscal years 2017-2019 (endnote 7).

questions.question: Which materials in iMac use 100 percent recycled content, and is any of these claims limited to a particular configuration?
questions.expected_answer: Aluminum (stand), copper (multiple PCBs and thermal module components), gold (PCB plating), rare earth elements (all magnets) and tin (PCB solder); the recycled copper in the thermal module applies to iMac (four ports) only (endnote 14).
evidence_phrases: representing 99 percent of the total rare earth
100 percent recycled gold in the plating
100 percent recycled tin in the solder

questions.question: How does the recycled content of iMac's packaging compare with the recycled content of the device itself?
questions.expected_answer: The fiber packaging contains 76 percent recycled content (p7, p8), while the device contains more than 15 percent recycled content (p1, p2, p5), a figure that excludes packaging (endnote 1).

questions.question: iMac uses 58 percent less energy than the ENERGY STAR requirement. What is that figure based on, and which power adapter was iMac tested with?
questions.expected_answer: It is based on the ENERGY STAR Program Requirements for Computers, including the maximum energy allowance for iMac; iMac was tested with the 143W Power Adapter, AC Cable (1m) and DC Cable (2m) (endnote 18).

questions.question: What share of iMac manufacturing electricity comes from low-carbon sources, and how is that percentage estimated?
questions.expected_answer: Over 20 percent (p1, p6). Apple attributes to its carbon model the low-carbon energy suppliers procured in the prior fiscal year, based on supplier manufacturing allocations at launch, assessing the suppliers for iMac (two ports) 256GB and counting only electricity procured through the Supplier Clean Energy Program (endnote 2).

questions.question: How much higher is the carbon footprint of iMac (four ports) 512GB than that of iMac (two ports) 256GB?
questions.expected_answer: 391 - 346 = 45 kg CO2e higher.

questions.question: By what percentage do emissions fall from the baseline to the final iMac emissions shown in the carbon neutral progress chart?
questions.expected_answer: (445 - 346) / 445 = about 22.2 percent, consistent with the 'more than 20 percent' claim.

questions.question: At 230V, how much more power does iMac draw in sleep mode than when it is off?
Approximately how many kg CO2e of the life cycle emissions of iMac (two ports) 256GB are attributable to production?
questions.expected_answer: About 173 kg CO2e (50% of 346 kg CO2e; percentages are rounded).

questions.question: What is the range of iMac's idle (display on) power consumption across the tested voltages?
questions.expected_answer: From 20.5W at 100V to 20.9W at 230V (20.6W at 115V).

questions.question: What is the power adapter's no-load power consumption at 100V, expressed in milliwatts?
What is the price of the iMac?
questions.expected_answer: Not in the report.

questions.question: How much does the iMac weigh?
questions.expected_answer: Not in the report.

questions.question: What was the carbon footprint of the 2023 iMac with the M3 chip?
questions.expected_answer: Not in the report (it covers the iMac introduced October 28, 2024).

questions.question: What is iMac's typical annual energy consumption in kWh?
questions.expected_answer: Not in the report (only mode power in watts and the 58% ENERGY STAR comparison).

questions.question: How much water is used to manufacture an iMac?
questions.expected_answer: Not in the report.

questions.question: What is the carbon footprint of iMac (four ports) with 1TB of storage?
questions.expected_answer: Not in the report (only two ports 256GB and four ports 512GB are given).

questions.question: What display resolution does the iMac have?
questions.expected_answer: Not in the report.
